title: C# Questions & Answers - Accessor controls of class
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers - Accessor controls of class - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on "Accessor controls of class".

questions.question: Which among these access specifiers should be used for main() method?
questions.explanation: The runtime can invoke Main whether it is public, internal, or private. No particular access modifier is required.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
Which of these access specifiers must be used for class so that it can be inherited by another subclass?
questions.explanation: A class does not have to be public to be inherited. A top-level class defaults to internal and can be a base class in the same assembly. Nested classes default to private and can still be inherited by other nested types in the same enclosing type.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are incorrect?

options.text: public members of class can be accessed by any code in the program
private members of class can only be accessed by other members of the class
private members of class can be inherited by a subclass, and become protected members in subclass
protected members of a class can be accessed from a derived class

questions.explanation: Private members are not accessible in a derived class and do not become protected. Public, private, and the corrected protected statement are true.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
Accessibility modifiers defined in a class are?

options.text: public, private, protected, internal, protected internal, private protected

questions.explanation: C# has six accessibility levels: public, private, protected, internal, protected internal, and private protected (C# 7.2 and later).
